{"figures":[{"fact_key":"total_return_on_starting_capital","value":396.26},{"fact_key":"benchmark_return","value":68.98},{"fact_key":"return_difference_versus_benchmark","value":327.27},{"fact_key":"starting_capital","value":1000.0},{"fact_key":"ending_portfolio_value","value":4962.59},{"fact_key":"highest_portfolio_value","value":6784.14},{"fact_key":"annualized_volatility","value":68.62},{"fact_key":"worst_drop_from_a_prior_high","value":-44.86},{"fact_key":"worst_drop_began","value":"2025-02-18"},{"fact_key":"worst_drop_ended","value":"2025-08-01"},{"fact_key":"portfolio_value_before_the_worst_drop","value":1747.1},{"fact_key":"portfolio_value_at_the_bottom_of_the_worst_drop","value":963.34},{"fact_key":"executed_fills","value":1}],"language":"en","text":"DOCN was an unusually strong holding over this test. A one-time purchase of $1,000 grew to $4,962.59, a total gain of 396.26%. That was $327.27 percentage points better than SPY’s 68.98% gain.

The main story was a series of changing expectations around DigitalOcean. In 2024, the company described steady growth in its core cloud business and very rapid growth in its artificial-intelligence products. It reported third-quarter revenue growth of 12% and raised its 2024 revenue outlook. Those results likely helped investors see DOCN as a company benefiting from the AI and cloud-computing boom, although that explanation is an inference about the stock’s move, not proof that any single event caused it.

Holding it was not a smooth ride. The portfolio’s annualized volatility was 68.62%, meaning its value tended to swing far more sharply than a broad-market fund. Its worst decline began on 2025-02-18 and ended on 2025-08-01. The portfolio fell from $1,747.10 to $963.34, a 44.86% drop from its previous high. In plain terms, an investor could have watched most of the earlier gains disappear and briefly seen the account below the original $1,000, even though the full-period result later became excellent.

The available reporting helps explain why confidence became less steady. DigitalOcean’s February 2025 results and outlook were better than some expectations, but commentary also highlighted concerns such as valuation and weaker cash-flow comparisons. Later reporting described a sizable decline from February into the summer. By August, the company was reporting stronger second-quarter results and raising its full-year revenue outlook. The evidence supports a period in which investors repeatedly reassessed growth, AI spending, profitability, and the price they were willing to pay for that growth. It does not establish that these events alone caused every move in DOCN.

SPY also benefited from a generally supportive market backdrop. Reuters reported that U.S. stocks reached records around the Federal Reserve’s September 2024 rate cut, while tariff concerns contributed to sharp market volatility in 2025. That broad-market support helps explain SPY’s positive result, but DOCN’s much larger gain means company-specific enthusiasm and risk mattered much more in this test.

Because there was only one executed fill, this was effectively a buy-and-hold test rather than a series of timed trades. The result shows the payoff from staying invested through both the large drawdown and the later recovery. It also shows the trade-off clearly: DOCN delivered far more than the benchmark, but getting there required tolerating much bigger swings and a temporary loss of nearly half the portfolio."}
